# 12 Parse interaction and styling directives

## Outcome

`parseClassDiagram` recognizes `click` (both `href` and `call` forms), `callback`, `link`,
`style`, `classDef` and `cssClass`, capturing them as structured declarations. The parser
validates syntax shape only — URL allowlisting and style-value rejection are ticket 13's job.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `click Shape href "https://example.com"` and the optional tooltip form
  (`click Shape href "url" "tooltip"`) parse into an interaction carrying target, url and tooltip.
- [ ] `click Shape call callbackFn()` and `click Shape call callbackFn("arg")` parse into an
  interaction carrying the function name and any literal argument.
- [ ] `callback Shape "callbackFn"` and `link Shape "https://example.com"` parse into the same
  interaction shapes as their `click` equivalents — they are spellings, not separate concepts.
- [ ] `style Shape fill:#fdd,stroke:#c00` parses into a style declaration carrying the target and
  an ordered list of `property: value` pairs.
- [ ] `classDef emphasis fill:#fdd` plus `cssClass "Shape,Other" emphasis` parse into a named style
  definition and an application naming both targets.
- [ ] A `javascript:` URL and a style value containing `url(` both **parse** without a diagnostic —
  they are syntactically valid; rejecting them is ticket 13's job at the model stage. Document this
  split in the implementation so it does not look like a missed check.
- [ ] Everything from tickets 01 and 07 still parses — their tests pass unmodified.
